title: T-03 - The Shadow Before Creation
claim: Evil is not a created substance; it is the away-direction made intelligible by the reality of the Good, made enterable by finite freedom, and made actual by creaturely refusal.
assumptions: Christian theology confesses God as wholly good, with no darkness in Him.
The distinction between possibility and actuality is valid and must be preserved.
Physics-side language about gradients, boundaries, state-space, openness, and noise is used as analogy/model language, not proof of sin.
definitions: Shadow: the possible away-direction implied by real orientation toward the Good.
Enterable shadow: the possibility of refusal once finite freedom exists.
Actualized evil: refusal of the Good by a free creature.

bridges.to: theological account of evil as parasitic refusal

negative_guards: Do not say God created evil as a substance.
Do not say evil is co-eternal with God.
Do not say physics proves the Fall.
Do not confuse finite dependence with moral evil.
kill_conditions: If possibility is treated as actuality, the argument fails.
If evil is made a positive substance in God or beside God, the argument fails.
If physics-side analogies are promoted to proof, the bridge label must be downgraded.
